resource.name: aws_instance
resource.description: Provides an EC2 instance resource. This allows instances to be created, updated, and deleted. Instances also support provisioning.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_instance` Terraform resource enables the creation, management, and lifecycle control of Amazon EC2 instances, providing a foundational building block for deploying virtual servers in AWS. Common use cases include hosting applications, setting up development or production environments, and provisioning compute resources for workloads. Users can configure key attributes such as instance type, AMI (Amazon Machine Image), networking (VPC, subnets, security groups), storage (EBS volumes), and advanced settings like user data scripts for bootstrapping, tags for resource organization, and auto-scaling integration.

examples.title: Basic example using AMI lookup
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_instance` resource using an AMI dynamically fetched via the `aws_ami` data source, with filters for the latest Ubuntu 22.04 image and Canonical ownership. Highlights the use of AMI lookup, instance type configuration (`t3.micro`), and tagging for resource identification."

examples.title: Spot instance example
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS EC2 spot instance using the `aws_instance` resource with `instance_market_options` to specify spot pricing and a maximum price (`max_price`). It also shows how to dynamically fetch the latest ARM64 Amazon Linux 2023 AMI using the `aws_ami` data source with filters, enabling cost-effective and optimized instance provisioning.

examples.title: Network and credit specification example
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_instance` with a custom network interface and unlimited CPU credits using the `network_interface` and `credit_specification` blocks. It also illustrates the setup of supporting resources, including a VPC, subnet, and network interface, to establish a private IP address and network connectivity for the instance.

examples.title: CPU options example
examples.llm_summary: This Terraform example demonstrates how to configure CPU options for an `aws_instance` resource, specifying `core_count` and `threads_per_core` for optimized performance. It also includes the setup of supporting resources like a VPC, subnet, and dynamic AMI selection to create a complete environment for deploying an Amazon Linux 2023 instance.

examples.title: Host resource group or License Manager registered AMI example
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_instance` resource to launch an EC2 instance using a License Manager registered AMI (`ami-0dcc1e21636832c5d`) with dedicated host tenancy and association to a specific host resource group (`host_resource_group_arn`). It illustrates the use of the `tenancy` and `host_resource_group_arn` arguments for deploying instances on a dedicated host in AWS.

arguments.name: ami
arguments.description: (Optional) AMI to use for the instance. Required unless `launch_template` is specified and the Launch Template specifes an AMI. If an AMI is specified in the Launch Template, setting `ami` will override the AMI specified in the Launch Template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ami` argument in the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that defines the operating system and pre-configured software for the EC2 instance. Setting this argument enables users to control the instance's base environment, ensuring it aligns with application requirements or deployment goals, and can override the AMI specified in a linked Launch Template if both are provided.

arguments.name: associate_public_ip_address
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to associate a public IP address with an instance in a VPC.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether the EC2 instance in a VPC is assigned a public IP address, enabling direct internet access without requiring additional networking configurations. Commonly used to configure instances for public-facing workloads or simplify connectivity in environments without NAT gateways or bastion hosts.

arguments.name: availability_zone
arguments.description: (Optional) AZ to start the instance in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `availability_zone` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the specific Availability Zone (AZ) within a region where the EC2 instance will be launched. This enables precise control over instance placement to optimize latency, redundancy, or proximity to other resources, supporting common goals like high availability and fault tolerance in cloud infrastructure design.

arguments.name: cpu_core_count
arguments.description: (Optional, Deprecated use the `cpu_options` argument instead) Sets the number of CPU cores for an instance. This option is only supported on creation of instance type that support CPU Options CPU Cores and Threads Per CPU Core Per Instance Type - specifying this option for unsupported instance types will return an error from the EC2 API.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of CPU cores for the EC2 instance during creation, allowing users to optimize compute performance for workloads on instance types that support CPU core and thread customization. Deprecated in favor of the `cpu_options` argument and may result in errors if used with unsupported instance types."

arguments.name: cpu_threads_per_core
arguments.description: (Optional - has no effect unless `cpu_core_count` is also set, Deprecated use the `cpu_options` argument instead) If set to 1, hyperthreading is disabled on the launched instance. Defaults to 2 if not set. See Optimizing CPU Options for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cpu_threads_per_core` argument in the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control the hyperthreading configuration of the instance's CPU by specifying the number of threads per core. Setting this argument to `1` disables hyperthreading, which can optimize performance for certain workloads, while the default value of `2` enables hyperthreading for increased parallelism. Note that this argument is deprecated and superseded by the `cpu_options` argument.

arguments.name: disable_api_stop
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, enables EC2 Instance Stop Protection.
arguments.llm_summary: The `disable_api_stop` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control EC2 Instance Stop Protection by specifying whether the instance can be stopped via API calls. Setting this to `true` prevents the instance from being stopped through the AWS API, which is useful for protecting critical workloads or ensuring high availability in production environments.

arguments.name: disable_api_termination
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, enables EC2 Instance Termination Protection.
arguments.llm_summary: The `disable_api_termination` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control the termination protection feature of an EC2 instance, preventing accidental deletion via API calls when set to `true`. This is commonly used to safeguard critical instances in production environments, ensuring they cannot be terminated without explicitly disabling this protection first.

arguments.name: ebs_optimized
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, the launched EC2 instance will be EBS-optimized. Note that if this is not set on an instance type that is optimized by default then this will show as disabled but if the instance type is optimized by default then there is no need to set this and there is no effect to disabling it. See the EBS Optimized section of the AWS User Guide for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ebs_optimized` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to enable or disable EBS optimization for the EC2 instance, which improves I/O performance for attached EBS volumes by dedicating additional bandwidth. This setting is typically used to optimize storage performance for workloads requiring high throughput or low latency, but it is unnecessary for instance types that are EBS-optimized by default.

arguments.name: enable_primary_ipv6
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to assign a primary IPv6 Global Unicast Address (GUA) to the instance when launched in a dual-stack or IPv6-only subnet. A primary IPv6 address ensures a consistent IPv6 address for the instance and is automatically assigned by AWS to the ENI. Once enabled, the first IPv6 GUA becomes the primary IPv6 address and cannot be disabled. The primary IPv6 address remains until the instance is terminated or the ENI is detached. Disabling `enable_primary_ipv6` after it has been enabled forces recreation of the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enable_primary_ipv6` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control whether a primary IPv6 Global Unicast Address (GUA) is automatically assigned to the instance's Elastic Network Interface (ENI) when launched in a dual-stack or IPv6-only subnet. Enabling this ensures the instance has a consistent IPv6 address for communication, supporting IPv6 networking requirements, but forces instance recreation if disabled after being set.

arguments.name: get_password_data
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, wait for password data to become available and retrieve it. Useful for getting the administrator password for instances running Microsoft Windows. The password data is exported to the `password_data` attribute. See GetPasswordData for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `get_password_data` argument in the `aws_instance` resource controls whether Terraform retrieves the administrator password for Windows instances by waiting for password data to become available. Enabling this functionality (`true`) allows users to access the `password_data` attribute, which is commonly used for securely obtaining initial login credentials for Windows-based environments.

arguments.name: hibernation
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, the launched EC2 instance will support hibernation.
arguments.llm_summary: The `hibernation` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to enable hibernation support for the EC2 instance, which preserves the instance's in-memory state when stopped, facilitating faster restarts and maintaining application state. This feature is useful for workloads requiring quick recovery or state retention across instance stops, aligning with goals like optimizing downtime and preserving session data.

arguments.name: host_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ID of a dedicated host that the instance will be assigned to. Use when an instance is to be launched on a specific dedicated host.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the specific dedicated host on which the instance will be launched, enabling users to control instance placement for scenarios requiring host-level isolation, resource optimization, or compliance with licensing and tenancy requirements."

arguments.name: host_resource_group_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the host resource group in which to launch the instances. If you specify an ARN, omit the `tenancy` parameter or set it to `host`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `host_resource_group_arn` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a host resource group to launch the instance on a dedicated host. By setting this argument, users can control the placement of the instance within a specific resource group, enabling configurations for tenancy optimization and compliance with dedicated hosting requirements.

arguments.name: iam_instance_profile
arguments.description: (Optional) IAM Instance Profile to launch the instance with. Specified as the name of the Instance Profile. Ensure your credentials have the correct permission to assign the instance profile according to the EC2 documentation, notably `iam:PassRole`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `iam_instance_profile` argument allows users to associate an IAM Instance Profile with the EC2 instance, enabling the instance to assume an IAM role and access AWS resources securely. By specifying the profile name, users can control permissions and policies for the instance, supporting common goals like managing access to S3, DynamoDB, or other AWS services without embedding credentials.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_instance` resource represents the unique identifier of the EC2 instance, typically assigned by AWS upon creation. While not required, it can be used to reference or track the instance programmatically, enabling users to query or manage the instance's state and attributes within Terraform workflows or external integrations.

arguments.name: instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior
arguments.description: (Optional) Shutdown behavior for the instance. Amazon defaults this to `stop` for EBS-backed instances and `terminate` for instance-store instances. Cannot be set on instance-store instances. See Shutdown Behavior for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define how the instance should behave when it is shut down from within the operating system. It configures whether the instance stops or terminates, enabling control over lifecycle management and resource retention for EBS-backed instances, while being inapplicable to instance-store instances.

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Instance type to use for the instance. Required unless `launch_template` is specified and the Launch Template specifies an instance type. If an instance type is specified in the Launch Template, setting `instance_type` will override the instance type specified in the Launch Template. Updates to this field will trigger a stop/start of the EC2 instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define the compute capacity and hardware configuration of the EC2 instance by specifying its type (e.g., `t2.micro`, `m5.large`). Setting this argument directly impacts the instance's performance, cost, and suitability for workloads, and it can override the instance type defined in a linked Launch Template if both are specified.

arguments.name: ipv6_address_count
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv6_address_count` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the instance's primary network interface. Configuring this argument enables IPv6 networking for the instance, supporting use cases like dual-stack environments, improved scalability, or compliance with modern networking requirements.

arguments.name: ipv6_addresses
arguments.description: (Optional) Specify one or more IPv6 addresses from the range of the subnet to associate with the primary network interface
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv6_addresses` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify one or more IPv6 addresses from the subnet's range to associate with the instance's primary network interface. This enables precise control over the instance's IPv6 networking configuration, supporting use cases like dual-stack environments, custom IP addressing, or compliance with specific network requirements.

arguments.name: key_name
arguments.description: (Optional) Key name of the Key Pair to use for the instance; which can be managed using the `aws_key_pair` resource.
arguments.llm_summary: The `key_name` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the name of an existing EC2 Key Pair to associate with the instance, enabling secure SSH access to the instance. By configuring this argument, users can define authentication credentials for remote management, aligning with common goals like securing administrative access to cloud servers.

arguments.name: monitoring
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, the launched EC2 instance will have detailed monitoring enabled. (Available since v0.6.0)
arguments.llm_summary: The `monitoring` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to enable or disable detailed monitoring for the EC2 instance. When set to `true`, it activates enhanced CloudWatch metrics collection, providing deeper insights into instance performance and resource utilization, which is useful for optimizing workloads and troubleshooting.

arguments.name: placement_group
arguments.description: (Optional) Placement Group to start the instance in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `placement_group` argument allows users to specify the name of a placement group in which the EC2 instance should be launched, enabling control over instance placement for optimized networking or workload distribution. This is commonly used to achieve high-performance computing goals, such as low-latency communication or clustered deployments, by grouping instances within a single logical unit.

arguments.name: placement_partition_number
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of the partition the instance is in. Valid only if the `aws_placement_group` resource's `strategy` argument is set to `"partition"`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `placement_partition_number` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the partition within a partition-based placement group where the instance will be launched. This configuration is relevant when the associated `aws_placement_group` uses the `partition` strategy, enabling users to optimize workload distribution and fault tolerance by isolating instances across distinct partitions within the placement group.

arguments.name: private_ip
arguments.description: (Optional) Private IP address to associate with the instance in a VPC.
arguments.llm_summary: The `private_ip` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify a custom private IP address for the instance within a VPC, enabling precise control over network configuration. By setting this argument, users can ensure the instance uses a specific private IP, which is useful for scenarios like static IP assignments, integration with existing network architectures, or maintaining predictable communication within private subnets.

arguments.name: secondary_private_ips
arguments.description: (Optional) List of secondary private IPv4 addresses to assign to the instance's primary network interface (eth0) in a VPC. Can only be assigned to the primary network interface (eth0) attached at instance creation, not a pre-existing network interface i.e., referenced in a `network_interface` block. Refer to the Elastic network interfaces documentation to see the maximum number of private IP addresses allowed per instance type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secondary_private_ips` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define additional private IPv4 addresses for the instance's primary network interface (`eth0`) during creation. This enables advanced network configurations, such as supporting multiple services or applications on distinct IPs within a VPC, and is particularly useful for scenarios requiring enhanced IP-based routing or segregation.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Optional, EC2-Classic and default VPC only) List of security group names to associate with. If you are creating Instances in a VPC, use vpc_security_group_ids instead.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_groups` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify a set of EC2 security group names to control network access to the instance in EC2-Classic or the default VPC. By defining this argument, users can manage inbound and outbound traffic rules for the instance, ensuring proper access control and security configurations for their application or workload.

arguments.name: source_dest_check
arguments.description: (Optional) Controls if traffic is routed to the instance when the destination address does not match the instance. Used for NAT or VPNs. Defaults true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `source_dest_check` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control whether the instance performs source/destination address validation on incoming traffic. Disabling this check (setting it to `false`) is essential for configuring instances as NAT gateways or VPN endpoints, enabling them to route traffic where the destination address does not match the instance itself.

arguments.name: subnet_id
arguments.description: (Optional) VPC Subnet ID to launch in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_id` argument allows users to specify the VPC subnet in which the EC2 instance will be launched, enabling control over the network placement and connectivity of the instance. By setting this argument, users can define the instance's association with specific routing, security groups, and IP address allocation within the chosen subnet, aligning with goals like isolating workloads or configuring network access.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the resource. Note that these tags apply to the instance and not block storage devices. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs that assign metadata to the instance, enabling organization, categorization, and identification of resources for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or automation workflows. These tags apply specifically to the instance itself (not associated block storage) and can override provider-level default tags if matching keys are present.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically merged from both provider-level and resource-specific tags. This enables consistent metadata management across AWS resources, supporting common goals like organizing instances by environment, cost allocation, or ownership for improved governance and operational clarity.

arguments.name: tenancy
arguments.description: (Optional) Tenancy of the instance (if the instance is running in a VPC). An instance with a tenancy of `dedicated` runs on single-tenant hardware. The `host` tenancy is not supported for the import-instance command. Valid values are `default`, `dedicated`, and `host`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tenancy` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify the instance's tenancy type within a VPC, controlling whether the instance runs on shared (`default`) or single-tenant (`dedicated`) hardware. This configuration impacts resource isolation and compliance, enabling users to meet specific performance or regulatory requirements, such as ensuring dedicated physical hardware for sensitive workloads.

arguments.name: user_data
arguments.description: (Optional) User data to provide when launching the instance. Do not pass gzip-compressed data via this argument; see `user_data_base64` instead. Updates to this field will trigger a stop/start of the EC2 instance by default. If the `user_data_replace_on_change` is set then updates to this field will trigger a destroy and recreate of the EC2 instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_data` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify a script or configuration data that is executed during the instance's initialization, enabling tasks such as setting environment variables, installing software, or configuring the operating system. Changes to this argument trigger a stop/start or, optionally, a destroy/recreate of the EC2 instance, making it ideal for defining instance-specific bootstrapping behavior.

arguments.name: user_data_base64
arguments.description: (Optional) Can be used instead of `user_data` to pass base64-encoded binary data directly. Use this instead of `user_data` whenever the value is not a valid UTF-8 string. For example, gzip-encoded user data must be base64-encoded and passed via this argument to avoid corruption. Updates to this field will trigger a stop/start of the EC2 instance by default. If the `user_data_replace_on_change` is set then updates to this field will trigger a destroy and recreate of the EC2 instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_data_base64` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify base64-encoded binary data for instance initialization, enabling the configuration of startup scripts or environment settings that are not valid UTF-8 strings (e.g., gzip-encoded data). Setting this argument ensures proper handling of non-textual user data and triggers instance lifecycle changes, such as stop/start or destroy/recreate, depending on the `user_data_replace_on_change` setting.

arguments.name: user_data_replace_on_change
arguments.description: (Optional) When used in combination with `user_data` or `user_data_base64` will trigger a destroy and recreate of the EC2 instance when set to `true`. Defaults to `false` if not set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_data_replace_on_change` argument in the `aws_instance` resource controls whether changes to the `user_data` or `user_data_base64` configuration trigger a forced destroy and recreation of the EC2 instance. This enables users to ensure lifecycle consistency for instances where updated initialization scripts or environment configurations require a clean state, supporting workflows that depend on immutable infrastructure principles.

arguments.name: volume_tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign, at instance-creation time, to root and EBS volumes. Do not use volume_tags if you plan to manage block device tags outside the aws_instance configuration, such as using tags in an aws_ebs_volume resource attached via aws_volume_attachment. Doing so will result in resource cycling and inconsistent behavior.
arguments.llm_summary: The `volume_tags` argument in the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define a map of tags that are automatically applied to the root and attached EBS volumes during instance creation. This enables streamlined resource organization, identification, and metadata management for storage volumes, but should not be used if block device tags are managed externally to avoid resource conflicts and cycling.

arguments.name: vpc_security_group_ids
arguments.description: (Optional, VPC only) List of security group IDs to associate with.
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_security_group_ids` argument for the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify a set of security group IDs to associate with the instance within a VPC. This configuration controls network-level access to the instance, enabling users to define inbound and outbound traffic rules for enhanced security and compliance with access policies.

blocks.name: capacity_reservation_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Describes an instance's Capacity Reservation targeting option. See Capacity Reservation Specification below for more details.  ami - (Optional) AMI to use for the instance. Required unless launch_template is specified and the Launch Template specifes an AMI. If an AMI is specified in the Launch Template, setting ami will override the AMI specified in the Launch Template.  associate_public_ip_address - (Optional) Whether to associate a public IP address with an instance in a VPC.  availability_zone - (Optional) AZ to start the instance in.  capacity_reservation_specification - (Optional) Describes an instance's Capacity Reservation targeting option. See Capacity Reservation Specification below for more details.  Changing cpu_core_count and/or cpu_threads_per_core will cause the resource to be destroyed and re-created.

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_preference
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates the instance's Capacity Reservation preferences. Can be `"open"` or `"none"`. (Default: `"open"`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_preference` argument in the `capacity_reservation_specification` block of the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define how the instance interacts with EC2 Capacity Reservations, specifying whether it should automatically use any open Capacity Reservations (`"open"`) or avoid them entirely (`"none"`). This configuration impacts instance placement and resource allocation, enabling users to optimize for availability or cost based on their workload requirements.

blocks.name: capacity_reservation_target
blocks.description: (Optional) Information about the target Capacity Reservation. See Capacity Reservation Target below for more details.  For more information, see the documentation on Capacity Reservations.

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ID of the Capacity Reservation in which to run the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_id` argument allows users to specify the ID of a Capacity Reservation in which the EC2 instance should run, enabling targeted allocation of compute capacity within a reserved pool. This configuration is typically used to ensure predictable instance availability in high-demand scenarios or reserved environments, aligning with capacity planning and resource management goals.

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_resource_group_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the Capacity Reservation resource group in which to run the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_resource_group_arn` argument allows users to specify the ARN of a Capacity Reservation resource group where the instance should run, enabling targeted allocation of compute capacity within a predefined reservation group. This configuration is useful for optimizing resource utilization and ensuring instances are launched in environments with reserved capacity, aligning with workload-specific requirements or cost management strategies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_target` block within the `capacity_reservation_specification` of the `aws_instance` resource defines settings to associate an EC2 instance with a specific Capacity Reservation, ensuring dedicated compute capacity for the instance. This block encapsulates configuration details for targeting a specific reservation, enabling users to optimize resource allocation and guarantee availability in high-demand scenarios.

The `capacity_reservation_specification` block in the `aws_instance` resource enables detailed control over an instance's targeting options for AWS Capacity Reservations, ensuring predictable resource availability in specific scenarios. It encapsulates settings related to Capacity Reservation preferences, allowing users to optimize instance placement and guarantee compute capacity for critical workloads.

blocks.name: cpu_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CPU options for the instance. See CPU Options below for more details.

arguments.name: amd_sev_snp
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to enable the instance for AMD SEV-SNP. AMD SEV-SNP is supported with M6a, R6a, and C6a instance types only. Valid values are `enabled` and `disabled`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `amd_sev_snp` argument within the `cpu_options` block of the `aws_instance` resource allows users to specify whether AMD SEV-SNP (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Secure Nested Paging) is enabled for the instance, enhancing hardware-based memory encryption and security. This feature is applicable only to specific instance types (M6a, R6a, C6a) and supports user goals related to configuring advanced security measures for workloads requiring confidential computing.

arguments.name: core_count
arguments.description: (Optional) Sets the number of CPU cores for an instance. This option is only supported on creation of instance type that support CPU Options CPU Cores and Threads Per CPU Core Per Instance Type - specifying this option for unsupported instance types will return an error from the EC2 API.
arguments.llm_summary: The `core_count` argument within the `cpu_options` block of the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define the number of physical CPU cores allocated to the instance during its creation. This configuration is useful for optimizing compute performance and tailoring the instance to workloads requiring specific core counts, but it is only applicable to instance types that support custom CPU options.

arguments.name: threads_per_core
arguments.description: (Optional - has no effect unless `core_count` is also set) If set to 1, hyperthreading is disabled on the launched instance. Defaults to 2 if not set. See Optimizing CPU Options for more information. For more information, see the documentation on Optimizing CPU options.
arguments.llm_summary: The `threads_per_core` argument in the `cpu_options` block of the `aws_instance` resource allows users to control the hyperthreading configuration of the instance's CPU. By setting this value to `1`, hyperthreading is disabled, optimizing the instance for workloads that benefit from single-threaded performance, while the default value of `2` enables hyperthreading for multi-threaded efficiency. This argument is typically used to fine-tune CPU performance based on workload requirements, such as high-performance computing or latency-sensitive applications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cpu_options` block in the `aws_instance` resource allows users to configure the CPU-related settings for an EC2 instance, such as the number of CPU cores and threads per core. This block provides fine-grained control over the instance's compute performance, enabling optimization for workloads that require specific CPU configurations, such as high-performance computing or multi-threaded applications.

blocks.name: credit_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for customizing the credit specification of the instance. See Credit Specification below for more details. Terraform will only perform drift detection of its value when present in a configuration. Removing this configuration on existing instances will only stop managing it. It will not change the configuration back to the default for the instance type.

arguments.name: cpu_credits
arguments.description: (Optional) Credit option for CPU usage. Valid values include `standard` or `unlimited`. T3 instances are launched as unlimited by default. T2 instances are launched as standard by default.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cpu_credits` argument in the `credit_specification` block of the `aws_instance` resource allows users to define the CPU credit configuration for burstable EC2 instances (e.g., T2 and T3). By specifying `standard` or `unlimited`, users can control whether the instance operates with capped CPU performance or can burst beyond baseline usage for higher workloads, aligning instance behavior with cost optimization or performance needs.

blocks.llm_summary: "Configures the credit specification for burstable performance instances within the `aws_instance` resource, allowing users to manage CPU credit usage and optimize cost-performance balance. This block encapsulates settings related to instance CPU behavior, enabling detailed control over whether the instance operates in standard or unlimited mode for handling workloads."

blocks.name: ebs_block_device
blocks.description: (Optional) One or more configuration blocks with additional EBS block devices to attach to the instance. Block device configurations only apply on resource creation. See Block Devices below for details on attributes and drift detection. When accessing this as an attribute reference, it is a set of objects.

arguments.name: delete_on_termination
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete_on_termination` argument for the `ebs_block_device` in the `aws_instance` resource controls whether the associated EBS volume is automatically deleted when the instance is terminated. Setting this to `true` ensures the volume is removed as part of the instance's lifecycle, supporting resource cleanup and cost management, while `false` retains the volume for data persistence beyond the instance's lifespan.

arguments.name: device_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `device_name` argument specifies the name of the block device to be attached to the instance, allowing users to define the mapping between the EBS volume and the instance's device identifier (e.g., `/dev/sda1`). By setting this argument, users ensure proper configuration of storage devices for the instance, enabling functionality such as persistent data storage or custom disk layouts.

arguments.name: encrypted
